notes: Drop rate: 44/248 = 17.7%. Higher than prior run's 10% because the broader source net (40 vs 14) pulled in more announcement-style content (hero-magazine recaps, popmatters album-reviews, indiewire pure reviews, embedded 'My Internet' format-repeats). The drop reasons cluster: pure reviews, brand campaigns, fair coverage, listicles, fiction/poetry, episode recaps. The forward-looking filter is calibrated tight per the disambiguation rules.

Substrate distribution skew: Status and Coping carry the largest pools, reflecting the source mix (literary quarterlies — Drift / n+1 / Baffler / Point — drive Coping and Agency; fashion/art magazines — 032c / Cultured / Polyester / Family Style — drive Status; entertainment — Variety / AvClub / Slate — split Status/Coping/Agency). Vitality and Connection are smaller but present.

Unsettled pool size: ~25 signals. The most generative material per the design doc principle. Includes the rupture-Maya Man-Christelle Oyiri cluster (032c + elephant.art), the etymology brainrot/Buddhism/symbiotic-virality/human-infohazards cluster, the food-and-kink piece (Vittles), the sinophobic-sinophilia and strange-pattern n+1 essays, and the queer-readings (final-girl-as-lesbian, kink-of-practice).

Confidence skew: many fit_confidence: medium calls reflect tagging from listing-page summaries rather than full-article reads, especially for elephant.art / family.style / 032c / hero / pinuphome where dates and per-article framing are partial.

Cross-pool drift to watch: 'Critic-recantation' (Slate's Lena Dunham revisit, the 2026 echo of 2024 Slate Sweeney piece dropped earlier) is recurring — could harden into its own forward-looking pattern next run if more critics stage public revisions. Worth flagging for Phase 2 generation.
